edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 11

source_text: Propterea adulescentulae dilexerunt te. Adulescentulae sunt animae nuper ad fidem venientes, quae odore nominis Christi attractae diligunt sponsum, nondum tamen ad perfectam caritatem pervenerunt. Dilexerunt, non diligunt in praesenti perfecte; promissio est et inchoatio. Quantum odor unguenti porrigitur, tantum adulescentulae currunt; cum exinanitum fuerit nomen in passione, tunc abundantius diligunt.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore young-women loved you. Young-women are souls recently unto faith coming, which by-fragrance of-name of-Christ having-been-drawn love bridegroom, not-yet however unto perfect charity have-arrived...
pass_b_english: [[Therefore the young women have loved you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. The young women are souls lately come to faith, drawn by the fragrance of Christ’s name to love the Bridegroom, yet not yet arrived at perfect charity. They have loved — not yet do they love perfectly in the present; it is promise and beginning. As far as the fragrance of the ointment reaches, so far the young women run; when the name has been emptied out in the passion, then they love more abundantly.
